newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Luxembourg PM sees Poland in EU by 2002.
newsitem.headline: Luxembourg PM sees Poland in EU by 2002.

text.p: Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker said on Tuesday that European Union enlargement into eastern Europe should not be delayed even if talks on a new EU treaty stretch past their mid-1997 deadline.
He also said Poland was likely to join the EU by 2002, two years after the date suggested by French President Jacques Chirac on a recent trip to Warsaw.

Juncker, speaking after meeting his Polish counterpart Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz, said Luxembourg's EU presidency in the second half of next year would speed up enlargement even if the EU's inter-governmental conference (IGC) was not over.
The IGC, a treaty review designed in part to prepare the EU for new members from eastern Europe and the Mediterranean, is due to finish in June next year at the end of the Netherlands' EU presidency.
Eastern European countries, including Poland, have been told that the EU would like to begin their membership negotiations six months after the end of the IGC.
"I see Poland in the EU by 2002," Juncker told a news conference.
"We will speed up the membership process," he said. "A delay in the IGC process could not delay the enlargement negotiations for Poland."
